title: 1. Urban Road Speed Limit (50 km/h)
summary: Default speed limit on urban roads without speed limit signs is 50 km/h.
canonical_question: If a motor vehicle driver exceeds the maximum speed limit by how many kilometers per hour or more, they shall be fined NT$6,000–36,000 and be prohibited from driving on the spot:

title: 2. Slow Lane & Narrow Road Speed Limit (40 km/h)
summary: Designated slow lanes and narrow roads without dividing lines have a max speed limit of 40 km/h.
key_fact: 2. Slow Lane & Narrow Road Speed Limit (40 km/h)
canonical_question: When driving into a 'national highway construction zone', which of the following driving behaviors is most effective in preventing accidents?
canonical_options: (1) Accelerate to overtake at the lane reduction point in the construction zone.
(2) Activate the driver assistance system (such as ACC/LTA) and then feel free to look at your phone.
(3) Change to the non-construction lane early, maintain a safe following distance, and stay fully focused and ready to brake at any time.
canonical_correct: (3) Change to the non-construction lane early, maintain a safe following distance, and stay fully focused and ready to brake at any time.

title: 3. Railroad Crossing Approach Speed (15 km/h)
summary: Approach railroad level crossings at 15 km/h or less and stop before crossing if red lights flash.
canonical_question: Can a U-turn be made on road sections with signs indicating curves, slopes, narrow roads, narrow bridges, tunnels, or at railroad level crossings?
canonical_options: (1) Yes.
(3) No special regulation.

title: 4. Downhill & Long Slope Engine Braking
summary: Use low gear engine braking on downhill slopes; avoid excessive foot braking to prevent brake fade.
canonical_question: When driving down a long slope, what is the correct driving method?
canonical_options: (1) Use the foot brake as much as possible to control speed.
(2) Do not use any brakes at all and let the vehicle coast naturally.
(3) Make good use of low gear engine braking and avoid excessive use of the foot brake.
canonical_correct: (3) Make good use of low gear engine braking and avoid excessive use of the foot brake.

title: 5. Speed vs. Braking Physics (Double Speed = 4x Distance)
summary: Braking distance is proportional to speed squared. Doubling speed quadruples required braking distance.
key_fact: 5. Speed vs. Braking Physics (Double Speed = 4x Distance)
canonical_question: When driving on a road and maintaining a safe following distance, if the vehicle ahead suddenly decelerates or brakes, what is the minimum safe following distance required?
canonical_options: (1) Enough for the driver's reaction distance plus braking distance.
(2) Enough for the driver's reaction distance only.
(3) Enough for the driver's braking distance only.
canonical_correct: (1) Enough for the driver's reaction distance plus braking distance.

title: 6. Breath Alcohol Administrative Limit (0.15 mg/L)
summary: Driving with breath alcohol concentration at or above 0.15 mg/L triggers mandatory administrative fines.
canonical_question: A motor vehicle driver's breath alcohol concentration must not reach, per liter:

title: 7. Criminal Drunk Driving Threshold (0.25 mg/L)
summary: BAC at or exceeding 0.25 mg/L constitutes a criminal offense under the Penal Code.
canonical_question: Regarding drunk driving regulations, which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) The standard for a breathalyzer test is a breath alcohol concentration of 0.25 mg per liter or a blood alcohol concentration of 0.10% or above.
(2) Re-offending drunk driving within 5 years is subject to a fine of NT$120,000.
(3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.
canonical_correct: (3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.

title: 8. Drunk Driving Administrative Fines (NT$30,000 ~ NT$120,000)
summary: Drunk driving for car drivers incurs fines from NT$30,000 to NT$120,000 plus license suspension.
canonical_question: Regarding drunk driving regulations, which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) The standard for a breathalyzer test is a breath alcohol concentration of 0.25 mg per liter or a blood alcohol concentration of 0.10% or above.
(2) Re-offending drunk driving within 5 years is subject to a fine of NT$120,000.
(3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.
canonical_correct: (3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.

title: 9. Repeat Drunk Driving within 10 Years
summary: Repeat drunk driving within 10 years results in maximum fines, license revocation, and public disclosure.
canonical_question: A driver commits drunk driving for the 3rd or more time within 10 years — which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) Only the fine amount is increased.
(2) An additional fine of NT$90,000 on top of the previous penalty shall be imposed, the driver's license shall be revoked, and the offender's name shall be publicly disclosed.
(3) Only demerit points are recorded.
canonical_correct: (2) An additional fine of NT$90,000 on top of the previous penalty shall be imposed, the driver's license shall be revoked, and the offender's name shall be publicly disclosed.

title: 10. Refusing Sobriety Breathalyzer Test (NT$180,000)
summary: Refusing a police breathalyzer test incurs an automatic NT$180,000 fine, impoundment, and license revocation.
canonical_question: Regarding drunk driving regulations, which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) The standard for a breathalyzer test is a breath alcohol concentration of 0.25 mg per liter or a blood alcohol concentration of 0.10% or above.
(2) Re-offending drunk driving within 5 years is subject to a fine of NT$120,000.
(3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.
canonical_correct: (3) Refusing a sobriety test for drunk driving is subject to a fine of NT$180,000, and the vehicle shall be impounded on the spot and the driver's license revoked.

title: 11. Passengers Joint Fine for Drunk Driving
summary: Passengers riding in a vehicle operated by an intoxicated driver are fined NT$6,000 to NT$15,000.
key_fact: 11. Passengers Joint Fine for Drunk Driving
canonical_question: A motor vehicle driver whose breath alcohol concentration reaches 0.25 mg per liter or blood alcohol concentration reaches 0.05% or above as determined by testing — for passengers in the same vehicle aged 18 and above but under 70, should they be penalized if there is no special reason? Which of the following statements is correct?
canonical_options: (1) Passengers in the same vehicle should be penalized.
(2) There is no penalty mechanism for passengers in the same vehicle.
(3) Passengers in the same vehicle do not need to be penalized as long as they have not consumed alcohol.
canonical_correct: (1) Passengers in the same vehicle should be penalized.

title: 12. Ignition Interlock Device (Alcohol Lock) Requirement
summary: Drivers re-applying after license revocation for drunk driving MUST install an approved ignition interlock device.
canonical_question: A driver whose license was previously revoked due to drunk driving must install what device in their vehicle before being allowed to drive after re-obtaining their license?
canonical_options: (1) A dashcam.
(2) A vehicle fire extinguisher.
(3) An ignition interlock device (alcohol lock).
canonical_correct: (3) An ignition interlock device (alcohol lock).

title: 13. Motorcycle Cargo Rear Extension (Max 50 cm)
summary: Motorcycle cargo must not extend forward past rider seat or more than 50 cm beyond rear wheel axle.

title: 14. Motorcycle Cargo Width Extension (Max 10 cm)

canonical_correct: (2) Cargo exceeds the prescribed length, width, or height, or is not covered tightly, causing scattered items to fall onto the road surface.

title: 15. Motorcycle Cargo Weight Limits (30kg / 60kg / 90kg)
summary: Motorcycle load weight limits: Small light = 30 kg; Regular light = 60 kg; Heavy = 90 kg.
canonical_question: Regarding regulations on vehicle cargo loading, which of the following constitutes 'improper conduct' subject to penalty?
canonical_options: (1) Cargo is securely tied and stably stacked.
(2) Cargo exceeds the prescribed length, width, or height, or is not covered tightly, causing scattered items to fall onto the road surface.
(3) The weight of loaded items does not exceed the approved gross weight.
canonical_correct: (2) Cargo exceeds the prescribed length, width, or height, or is not covered tightly, causing scattered items to fall onto the road surface.

title: 16. Small Vehicle Cargo Height (Max 2.85m / 1.5x width)
summary: Car cargo height must not exceed 1.5 times vehicle width or a maximum height of 2.85 meters.
canonical_question: When a small truck (not a van-type cargo vehicle) is loaded with goods, what is the maximum loading height from ground level permitted by law?
canonical_options: (1) 2 meters.
(2) 2.5 meters.
(3) 2.85 meters.
canonical_correct: (3) 2.85 meters.

title: 17. Cargo Protrusion & Falling Spills Penalty
summary: Cargo must be tightly covered and secured. Items spilling onto roads incur severe fines and demerit points.
canonical_question: Regarding regulations on vehicle cargo loading, which of the following constitutes 'improper conduct' subject to penalty?
canonical_options: (1) Cargo is securely tied and stably stacked.
(2) Cargo exceeds the prescribed length, width, or height, or is not covered tightly, causing scattered items to fall onto the road surface.
(3) The weight of loaded items does not exceed the approved gross weight.
canonical_correct: (2) Cargo exceeds the prescribed length, width, or height, or is not covered tightly, causing scattered items to fall onto the road surface.

title: 18. Straight Vehicles Priority over Turning Vehicles
summary: Vehicles going straight have absolute priority over vehicles turning into the same lane or intersection.
key_fact: 18. Straight Vehicles Priority over Turning Vehicles
canonical_question: When a vehicle is turning, which of the following is INCORRECT?
canonical_options: (1) A motor vehicle on a road with two or more same-direction lanes shall not drive in the inner lane except when preparing to turn left.
(2) At an intersection with dedicated left-turn or right-turn lanes, straight-through vehicles shall not occupy the dedicated turning lanes.
(3) At an unsignalized intersection where both roads have the same number of lanes, turning vehicles shall stop and yield to straight-through vehicles.
canonical_correct: (1) A motor vehicle on a road with two or more same-direction lanes shall not drive in the inner lane except when preparing to turn left.

title: 19. Left-Turn vs. Right-Turn Priority
summary: When vehicles from opposite directions turn into the same lane, left-turning vehicles yield to right-turning vehicles.
canonical_question: When approaching an unmarked intersection without a division between major and minor roads, if a car driver intends to turn left while an oncoming vehicle is simultaneously turning right into the same lane, which of the following statements is correct?
canonical_options: (1) The larger vehicle has the right of way; the smaller vehicle should yield.
(2) The left-turning vehicle should yield to the right-turning vehicle.
(3) The right- turning vehicle should yield to the left-turning vehicle.
canonical_correct: (3) The right- turning vehicle should yield to the left-turning vehicle.

title: 20. Unsignalized Equal Width Intersection Priority
summary: At unsignalized intersections of equal width, drivers yield to vehicles approaching from their right side.
canonical_question: The intersecting crosswalk marking at the intersection is:
canonical_options: (1) Diagonal pedestrian crossing line.
(2) Grid line.
(3) Bicycle crossing line.
canonical_correct: (1) Diagonal pedestrian crossing line.

title: 21. Branch Road vs. Main Road Priority
summary: Vehicles entering from side/branch roads must stop and yield right-of-way to main road traffic.
key_fact: 21. Branch Road vs. Main Road Priority
canonical_question: When a vehicle reaches an unsigned intersection and a vehicle on a secondary road encounters a vehicle on a main road, which of the following correctly states the right-of-way rule?
canonical_options: (1) The secondary road vehicle must yield to the main road vehicle.
(2) It depends on the speed of both vehicles; the faster one goes first.
(3) As long as the main road vehicle is still far away, the secondary road vehicle may proceed directly through the intersection.
canonical_correct: (1) The secondary road vehicle must yield to the main road vehicle.

title: 22. Pedestrian Crosswalk Priority (3 Meters / 4 Stripes)
summary: Drivers MUST stop at least 3 meters (4 zebra stripes) before crosswalks to yield to pedestrians.
canonical_question: A driver at an intersection sees a green light and prepares to turn left. At this moment, pedestrians are still slowly crossing on the pedestrian crosswalk markings. Which of the following behaviors is correct? --- PAGE 38 ---
canonical_options: (1) Stop about 3 meters in front of the pedestrians and remain completely stationary until they have passed.
(2) Slowly glide toward the pedestrians, and once they have walked past the center line, accelerate and pass behind them.
(3) As long as the pedestrians have not yet walked into your intended path, you may maintain your speed and turn.
canonical_correct: (1) Stop about 3 meters in front of the pedestrians and remain completely stationary until they have passed.

title: 23. Roundabout Traffic Priority
summary: Vehicles entering roundabouts MUST yield right-of-way to vehicles already inside the roundabout.
canonical_question: (1) Roundabout direction. (2) Divided road. (3) One-way road.
canonical_options: (1) Roundabout direction.
(2) Divided road.
(3) One-way road.
canonical_correct: (1) Roundabout direction.

title: 24. Yielding to Emergency Vehicles & Sirens
summary: Drivers MUST pull right and yield immediately to emergency sirens. Failure results in license revocation.
canonical_question: When a motor vehicle is traveling on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction, in addition to following signs and markings, which of the following behaviors is correct?
canonical_options: (1) When changing lanes, yield to vehicles going straight and maintain a safe following distance.
(2) When a small vehicle is traveling slowly, it should travel in the outer lane but may change lanes freely.
(3) An ambulance on an emergency call should travel in the inner lane.
canonical_correct: (1) When changing lanes, yield to vehicles going straight and maintain a safe following distance.

title: 25. Solid Red Line (No Stopping 24 Hours)
summary: Solid red roadside lines prohibit temporary stopping or parking 24 hours a day.
canonical_question: Regarding the 'solid red line' (no stopping line) marked on the roadside, what is the general prohibition period for temporary stopping?
canonical_options: (1) Only from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily.
(2) Unless otherwise specified, the general rule is 24 hours a day.
(3) Only during nighttime hours to maintain traffic safety.
canonical_correct: (2) Unless otherwise specified, the general rule is 24 hours a day.

title: 26. Solid Yellow Line (No Parking 7 AM - 8 PM)
summary: Solid yellow lines prohibit parking from 7 AM to 8 PM; temporary stopping (<3 mins) is permitted.
key_fact: 26. Solid Yellow Line (No Parking 7 AM - 8 PM)
canonical_question: What does a solid yellow line marked at the edge of the road indicate?
canonical_options: (1) No stopping line (equivalent to a red curb; temporary stopping is prohibited).
(2) No parking line (yellow line; brief temporary stopping is --- PAGE 66 --- permitted).
(3) Yield line.
canonical_correct: (2) No parking line (yellow line; brief temporary stopping is --- PAGE 66 --- permitted).

title: 27. Double Solid Yellow Lines (No Crossing / No U-Turn)
summary: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions. Crossing or U-turning over them is strictly illegal.
key_fact: 27. Double Solid Yellow Lines (No Crossing / No U-Turn)
canonical_question: A driver traveling on a road marked with a double solid yellow center line (directional restriction line) wishes to turn left into a lane on the opposite side. What should the driver do?
canonical_options: (1) After activating the left turn signal, the driver may cross the double solid yellow line and turn left into the lane.
(2) The driver must not cross the double solid yellow line and should find another appropriate legal intersection to make a U-turn or take a detour.
(3) When the vehicle speed is below 20 km/h, the driver may briefly cross the double solid yellow line to turn left.
canonical_correct: (2) The driver must not cross the double solid yellow line and should find another appropriate legal intersection to make a U-turn or take a detour.

title: 28. Inverted White Triangle Road Marking (Yield Line)
summary: An inverted white triangle marked on the road surface indicates a Yield Line requiring drivers to slow and yield.
key_fact: 28. Inverted White Triangle Road Marking (Yield Line)
canonical_question: The white inverted triangle road marking shown is:
canonical_options: (1) Yield line.
(2) Stop line.
(3) Road obstacle line.
canonical_correct: (1) Yield line.

title: 29. Flashing Red vs. Flashing Yellow Signal
summary: Flashing Red = Complete stop before proceeding. Flashing Yellow = Slow down and proceed with caution.
key_fact: 29. Flashing Red vs. Flashing Yellow Signal
canonical_question: When changing lanes while driving, if the turn signal is not displayed throughout the entire maneuver as --- PAGE 2 --- required, what is the regulation?
canonical_options: (1) Regardless of whether it is a regular road or a highway, it is a violation and should be penalized according to the law.
(2) It is only a violation when driving on a highway.
(3) As long as there are no vehicles approaching from behind, not displaying the turn signal carries no penalty.
canonical_correct: (1) Regardless of whether it is a regular road or a highway, it is a violation and should be penalized according to the law.

title: 30. Police Officer Direction Superiority
summary: Manual directions given by a police officer on site override all automated signals or road signs.
canonical_question: When a motor vehicle driver approaches an intersection and encounters a situation where a police officer's directions conflict with the traffic signal, how should the driver proceed?
canonical_options: (1) Follow the traffic signal.
(2) Follow the police officer's directions.
(3) Follow the vehicle ahead based on the current traffic conditions.
canonical_correct: (2) Follow the police officer's directions.

title: 31. Turn Signal Advance Distance (30 Meters)
summary: Activate turn signals at least 30 meters before turning or changing lanes on city streets.
canonical_question: When a driver reaches an intersection and proceeds or turns, which of the following regulations is correct?
canonical_options: (1) When turning right from the slow lane, change into the slow lane at a point 20 to 40 meters from the intersection.
(2) When turning right, the turn signal should be activated 50 meters before the intersection.
(3) When turning right from the outer lane, the turn signal should be activated 30 meters before the intersection.
canonical_correct: (3) When turning right from the outer lane, the turn signal should be activated 30 meters before the intersection.

title: 32. Overtaking Regulations & Prohibited Locations
summary: Overtake on the left side only. Overtaking is prohibited in tunnels, bridges, curves, or level crossings.
canonical_question: (1) No overtaking. (2) No oncoming traffic. (3) No motor vehicles allowed.
canonical_options: (1) No overtaking.
(2) No oncoming traffic.
(3) No motor vehicles allowed.
canonical_correct: (1) No overtaking.

title: 33. Prohibited U-Turn Locations
summary: U-turns are prohibited on sharp curves, steep slopes, narrow bridges, tunnels, or over double yellow lines.
canonical_question: Can a U-turn be made on road sections with signs indicating curves, slopes, narrow roads, narrow bridges, tunnels, or at railroad level crossings?
canonical_options: (1) Yes.
(3) No special regulation.

title: 34. Reversing & Backing Up Restrictions
summary: Reversing is prohibited on steep slopes, sharp curves, narrow roads, or expressways.
canonical_question: While driving, which of the following is correct regarding the use of display devices within the driver's field of vision?
canonical_options: (1) In-vehicle audio-visual devices may be used while driving as long as the sound is muted.
(2) Entertainment display devices should be turned off, but driving assistance displays such as navigation --- PAGE 6 --- or reversing cameras may be used.
(3) All display devices must be turned off to avoid distracting the driver.
canonical_correct: (2) Entertainment display devices should be turned off, but driving assistance displays such as navigation --- PAGE 6 --- or reversing cameras may be used.

title: 35. Handheld Mobile Device Penalties (Car NT$3,000 / Moto NT$1,000)
summary: Operating handheld mobile phones while driving incurs fines of NT$3,000 for cars and NT$1,000 for motorcycles.
key_fact: 35. Handheld Mobile Device Penalties (Car NT$3,000 / Moto NT$1,000)
canonical_question: A motor vehicle driver on a freeway or expressway who uses flashing lights or continuous honking to force the vehicle ahead to yield — which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) Reminding the vehicle ahead to yield is not a violation.
(2) A fine of not less than NT$3,000 and not more than NT$6,000 shall be imposed.
(3) No penalty applies as long as no accident occurs.
canonical_correct: (2) A fine of not less than NT$3,000 and not more than NT$6,000 shall be imposed.

title: 36. Cigarette Smoking While Driving Fine (NT$1,200)
summary: Holding, smoking, or lighting a cigarette while driving that affects others incurs a fine of NT$1,200.
canonical_question: Regarding a motor vehicle driver who holds, smokes, or lights a cigarette while driving and poses a risk to others' safety, which of the following is correct?
canonical_options: (1) It is a personal habit and not subject to punishment.
(2) It violates the Road Traffic Management Penalty Act and is subject to a fine of NT$1,200.
(3) It is a matter of violating environmental protection regulations.
canonical_correct: (2) It violates the Road Traffic Management Penalty Act and is subject to a fine of NT$1,200.

title: 37. Freeway Small Car Following Distance (Speed ÷ 2 in meters)
summary: Freeway following distance for small cars: Speed (km/h) ÷ 2 = Minimum safe distance in meters.
key_fact: 37. Freeway Small Car Following Distance (Speed ÷ 2 in meters)
canonical_question: When driving into a 'national highway construction zone', which of the following driving behaviors is most effective in preventing accidents?
canonical_options: (1) Accelerate to overtake at the lane reduction point in the construction zone.
(2) Activate the driver assistance system (such as ACC/LTA) and then feel free to look at your phone.
(3) Change to the non-construction lane early, maintain a safe following distance, and stay fully focused and ready to brake at any time.
canonical_correct: (3) Change to the non-construction lane early, maintain a safe following distance, and stay fully focused and ready to brake at any time.

title: 38. Freeway Innermost Lane Usage (Overtaking Only)
summary: The innermost freeway lane is the overtaking lane; non-overtaking vehicles must travel at max legal speed.
canonical_question: When a small vehicle is traveling on a freeway or expressway and does not impede traffic flow, it may travel at the maximum speed limit of that road section in the overtaking lane. Which of the following is the overtaking lane on a freeway or expressway?
canonical_options: (1) The innermost lane.
(2) The outermost lane.
(3) The middle lane.
canonical_correct: (1) The innermost lane.

title: 39. Hard Shoulder Driving Restrictions
summary: Driving on freeway hard shoulders is prohibited except during breakdowns, emergencies, or opened shoulder signs.
canonical_question: The freeway shoulder (outer shoulder) is open for driving during specific periods. Which of the following rules regarding shoulder use is incorrect?
canonical_options: (1) To avoid congestion on the main lanes ahead, you may merge onto the shoulder at any time.
(2) When driving on an open shoulder, you should merge back onto the main lane in an orderly manner before the end point.
(3) If not officially announced as open, the shoulder is only for use by ambulances, fire trucks, and official duty vehicles.
canonical_correct: (1) To avoid congestion on the main lanes ahead, you may merge onto the shoulder at any time.

title: 40. Warning Triangle Distance (100 Meters on Freeway)
summary: Place warning triangles at least 100 meters behind broken-down vehicles on freeways (30-100m on regular roads).
key_fact: 40. Warning Triangle Distance (100 Meters on Freeway)
canonical_question: When a vehicle breaks down and cannot be driven, it should be moved to a location that does not obstruct traffic. Regarding the handling of breakdown warning signs before or after the vehicle is moved, which of the following is incorrect?
canonical_options: (1) On roads with a speed limit of 40 km/h or below, the sign should be placed on the road surface 100 meters behind the vehicle; placement at an appropriate position in front of the vehicle may be set as needed.

(2) On roads with a speed limit exceeding 40 km/h, the sign should be placed on the road surface between 30 and 100 meters behind the vehicle; placement at an appropriate position in front of the vehicle may be set as needed.
(3) On congested road sections, the sign should be hung on the rear of the vehicle; placement at an appropriate position in front of the vehicle may be set as needed.
canonical_correct: (1) On roads with a speed limit of 40 km/h or below, the sign should be placed on the road surface 100 meters behind the vehicle; placement at an appropriate position in front of the vehicle may be set as needed.

title: 41. Tire Tread Depth Standards (1.6mm Car / 1.0mm Moto)
summary: Minimum tire tread depth is 1.6 mm for cars and 1.0 mm for motorcycles. Worn tires risk aquaplaning.
key_fact: 41. Tire Tread Depth Standards (1.6mm Car / 1.0mm Moto)
canonical_question: Which of the following statements about tire maintenance is correct?
canonical_options: (1) Regularly check tire pressure; maintaining proper tire pressure can reduce fuel consumption and extend tire life.
(2) Once the tire tread wears down to the tread wear indicator, keep driving as long as there is no blowout.
(3) The higher the tire pressure, the more fuel-efficient, so tires should be inflated to the maximum limit.
canonical_correct: (1) Regularly check tire pressure; maintaining proper tire pressure can reduce fuel consumption and extend tire life.

title: 42. Mandatory Seatbelt & Child Safety Seat Laws
summary: All occupants MUST wear seatbelts. Children under 4 years old must sit in rear-facing child safety seats.
key_fact: 42. Mandatory Seatbelt & Child Safety Seat Laws
canonical_question: (1) No vehicles allowed. (2) No cars (4+ wheels) or motorcycles allowed. (3) No pedestrians allowed.
canonical_options: (1) No vehicles allowed.
(2) No cars (4+ wheels) or motorcycles allowed.
(3) No pedestrians allowed.
canonical_correct: (2) No cars (4+ wheels) or motorcycles allowed.

title: 43. Door Opening 2-Stage Protocol
summary: Always use 2-stage door opening: check mirrors, check blind spots, open door slightly, then step out safely.
canonical_question: The 'two-stage door opening method' means:
canonical_options: (1) Open the door in two stages without checking for traffic or pedestrians.
(2) First open the door slightly, check for traffic and pedestrians, then open fully.
(3) Both of the above.
canonical_correct: (2) First open the door slightly, check for traffic and pedestrians, then open fully.

title: 44. Periodic Vehicle Inspection Frequency
summary: Cars >5 years old require annual inspection; cars >10 years old require inspection twice per year.
canonical_question: Private small passenger vehicles with license plates (except those using LPG or CNG) must be inspected:
canonical_options: (1) Exempt from periodic inspection if less than 5 years old; at least once per year if 5 to 10 years old; at least twice per year if over 10 years old.
(2) At least 3 times per year if over 10 years old.
(3) At least twice per year if less than 5 years old.
canonical_correct: (1) Exempt from periodic inspection if less than 5 years old; at least once per year if 5 to 10 years old; at least twice per year if over 10 years old.

title: 45. Compulsory Automobile Liability Insurance
summary: All motor vehicles must carry active Compulsory Liability Insurance; driving without it incurs impoundment.
canonical_question: If a motor vehicle driver removes the muffler, causing noise pollution, the driver shall be fined, prohibited from driving on the spot, and have the vehicle license plates suspended for six months. If the offense is repeated within one year, the penalty shall be:
canonical_options: (1) Revocation of the driver’s license
(2) Suspension of the driver’s license for one month
(3) Suspension of the driver’s license for six months ▸  Other (Railway Crossings, Compulsory Insurance, Eco-Driving, Weather, Driving Ethics)
canonical_correct: (3) Suspension of the driver’s license for six months ▸  Other (Railway Crossings, Compulsory Insurance, Eco-Driving, Weather, Driving Ethics)

title: 46. First Aid Treatment Order (Airway -> Bleeding -> Fracture)
summary: First aid priority order: 1. Open Airway (B). 2. Control Bleeding (A). 3. Immobilize Fractures (C).
key_fact: 46. First Aid Treatment Order (Airway -> Bleeding -> Fracture)
canonical_question: (1) First-aid station. (2) Gas station. (3) Repair station.
canonical_options: (1) First-aid station.
(2) Gas station.
(3) Repair station.
canonical_correct: (3) Repair station.

title: 47. CPR Chest Compression Ratio & Rate (30:2 / 100-120 bpm)
summary: Adult CPR standard: 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths at a rate of 100-120 compressions per minute.
key_fact: 47. CPR Chest Compression Ratio & Rate (30:2 / 100-120 bpm)
canonical_question: If the owner of a vehicle knowingly allows a driver to operate the vehicle while the driver's blood alcohol concentration exceeds the legal limit, or while under the influence of drugs or hallucinogens, and fails to prohibit such driving, in addition to a fine under the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act, what action will be taken against the vehicle?
canonical_options: (1) Suspension of the vehicle's license plates for 6 months
(2) Suspension of the vehicle's license plates for 1 year
(3) Suspension of the vehicle's license plates for 2 years
canonical_correct: (3) Suspension of the vehicle's license plates for 2 years
